sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the central part of Maple Shade, Burlington County, at 50 feet to an inch, with Camden Avenue (the main street, now Main Street) crossing the middle of the sheet from side to side. North of Camden Avenue the sheet shows two large blocks between Terrace Avenue, Lippincott Avenue and the diagonal Fork Landing Road (also lettered Central Avenue). The western block is a regular grid of narrow lots with dwellings and a few outbuildings. The eastern block, between Lippincott Avenue and Fork Landing Road, is mostly vacant lots divided by Myrtle Avenue (marked not opened) and a private alley, with the lumber and coal yard of J. S. Collins and Son and the premises of the Aero Radio Corporation and E. Brubaker and Son, shirt makers, in its upper right corner beside a railroad siding. Front Avenue and the Camden and Burlington County Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) run along the top of the sheet. A small church, the Bethel Pentecostal Church, and a service station with a battery shop stand at the right edge on Fork Landing Road and Camden Avenue. South of Camden Avenue Lippincott Avenue runs diagonally and a block of dwellings lies between it, Margaret Avenue and Helen Avenue, with another private alley; the area west of Lippincott Avenue is blank, belonging to Sheet 7. Water pipes (4, 6 and 8 inch) are marked along most streets and the sheet carries a compass rose, a scale bar and the oval Maple Shade stamp.
notes: Camden Avenue is now East Main Street and West Main Street, divided at Forklanding Road.
Front Avenue is now West Front Street; Fork Landing Road (Central Avenue) is now North and South Forklanding Road.
Fork Landing Road is lettered with the alternative name Central Avenue; Myrtle Avenue and the private alley are marked not opened.
Scale bar reads 50 ft to one inch; the fit gives about 7.9 px/ft, consistent with the other 50 ft sheets.
Terrace Avenue jogs about 30 ft at Camden Avenue, so the junction there is not a clean crossing.
The sheet's Nagle Avenue (west of Lippincott Avenue) corresponds to the modern Helen Avenue; the sheet's Helen Avenue at the bottom corresponds to modern Helen Avenue east of Lippincott.

50 ft to an inch. Centre of town on Camden Av (East/West Main Street) with Front Av, Terrace, Lippincott, Margaret Avs and Fork Landing Rd (Central Av); one part. The sheet Nagle Av is modern Helen Avenue west of Lippincott.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 is the commercial centre of Maple Shade, at 50 feet to an inch, with the crossing of Camden Avenue (now Main Street) and Fork Landing Road (also lettered Central Avenue) near its middle. The upper left shows a residential district laid out at an angle along Fork Landing Road, between Front Avenue, Theodore Avenue and Wallace Avenue, with dwellings, a Congregational church and a paint shop. On the north side of Camden Avenue stand a row of stores, a movie house with a balcony, a bakery and an auto repair garage, and further north on Maple Avenue the Maple Shade Public School No. 1, a large brick school with two wings. The right side carries Maple Avenue and Poplar Avenue as long north-south streets with dwellings scattered on large lots. South of Camden Avenue the sheet shows the main shopping frontage with stores, a bank, drugs, the Maple Shade Municipal Building with an auditorium and fire department, a post office, a tin shop and Barlow and Company, and the wagon and truck body works of Wm. Frech Co. at Spruce Avenue. Helen Avenue forms the bottom edge. Water pipes are marked in most streets, a compass rose sits at the left and the scale bar is in the centre bottom. Railroad sidings of the Camden and Burlington County Railroad appear at the top left corner.
notes: Camden Avenue is now East Main Street and West Main Street, divided at Forklanding Road.
Front Avenue is now East Front Street; Maple Avenue and Poplar Avenue north of Camden Avenue are now North Maple Avenue and North Poplar Avenue.
East Main Street junctions east of Forklanding Road (Maple, Spruce and Poplar) carried residuals of 2 to 4 m and were excluded; the fit rests on Forklanding Road and Front Avenue junctions.
Margaret Avenue / Main Street was rejected at 12.8 m (the drawn street is narrower than the modern one) and Margaret Avenue was left out of the street list.
Scale bar reads 50 ft to one inch; fitted scale about 7.93 px/ft.

50 ft to an inch. Commercial centre: Front Av and Station Av to Camden Av between Fork Landing Rd (Central Av) and Poplar Av; one part. Control lies along Forklanding Road and Front Avenue only; East Main Street junctions east of Forklanding left out (2-4 m).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 lies east of Sheet 3 and shows the district south of Camden Avenue (now Main Street), at 50 feet to an inch. The streets here run diagonally: Spruce Avenue, Poplar Avenue and Fellowship Road run from upper left to lower right, crossed by East Avenue, Maple Avenue and Center Avenue at right angles. Spruce Avenue also runs straight down the left edge near the top before turning diagonal. The blocks are narrow lots mostly occupied by single dwellings with outbuildings, with a contractors' yard marked between Poplar Avenue and Spruce Avenue. In the upper part stand the Immanuel Baptist Church, and the Church of Our Lady of Perpetual Help (Roman Catholic), a large masonry church shown in pink and marked as taken from plans. Along Camden Avenue at the top right is a block of stores built of cinder block, with a printing shop and dwellings beside it, and a short run of lots along Chestnut Avenue at the right edge. Street widths of 50 feet are marked along most streets, with water pipes lettered in several. A compass rose and a north arrow sit in the upper middle, the scale bar and Map Division stamp are at the bottom, and the oval Maple Shade stamp is at the upper right.
notes: Camden Avenue is now East Main Street; East Avenue is now East Gradwell Avenue.

Spruce Avenue, South Poplar Avenue, South Maple Avenue and Center Avenue (East Center Avenue) keep their names; Fellowship Road is now South Fellowship Road and Chestnut Avenue is South Chestnut Avenue.
Scale bar reads 50 ft to one inch; fitted scale about 7.97 px/ft, rotation about 7 degrees.
The church at the top centre is marked 'From Plans'.
50 ft to an inch. Diagonal streets south of Camden Av: Spruce, Maple, Poplar, Fellowship Rd, Chestnut, East Av (East Gradwell Avenue), Center Av; one part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 lies south of Camden Avenue (now Main Street) in the eastern part of Maple Shade, at 50 feet to an inch. A regular grid of north-south streets, Chestnut Avenue, Cherry Avenue, Walnut Avenue and Holly Avenue, runs down the sheet from Camden Avenue to Maple Heights Avenue and continues below it, with blocks of narrow numbered lots almost entirely holding single dwellings and small outbuildings, a few stores and a pink-and-blue building on Chestnut Avenue at the top left. A diagonal group of streets crosses the lower left: Fellowship Road runs from upper left to lower right through the middle, Poplar Avenue lies along its western side and Center Avenue crosses them from lower left to upper right. Several blocks between these diagonal streets contain dwellings and coops, and a few large dwellings stand beyond the street grid. At the upper right is a frame dwelling drawn in blue and a Maple Shade oval stamp. Water pipes (4 and 6 inch) are shown along most streets and building numbers are written along the lot lines. A compass rose and north arrow are at the left edge, and the scale bar with the Map Division stamp are at the bottom.
notes: Camden Avenue is now East Main Street; Maple Heights Avenue is now Maple Heights Road.
Chestnut, Walnut and Holly Avenues are now South Chestnut Avenue, South Walnut Avenue and South Holly Avenue; Fellowship Road is South Fellowship Road and Poplar Avenue is South Poplar Avenue.
Scale bar reads 50 ft to one inch; fitted scale about 7.92 px/ft, rotation about 7.6 degrees.
50 ft to an inch. Grid south of Camden Av between Chestnut and Holly Avs, Maple Heights Av, Fellowship Rd, Center Av; one part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers a residential block of Maple Shade south of Camden Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned slightly from north. Camden Avenue runs along the top edge, and Maple Heights Avenue crosses the sheet just above its middle. Holly Avenue, Pine Avenue, Cedar Avenue and Boulevard Avenue run north to south between them; south of Maple Heights Avenue the sheet continues down Holly, Pine and Cedar Avenues to the diagonal Boulevard Avenue, which crosses the lower right corner with the short Bailey, Salmon and Foster Avenues meeting it. The blocks are numbered 113 to 116 north of Maple Heights Avenue and 141 to 143 south of it. Almost every lot holds a detached frame dwelling with a small auto garage behind it, set back at a regular distance from the street; the frontages along Camden Avenue are a row of similar houses. A photo studio stands on Cedar Avenue in block 115, and two brick-veneered or tiled dwellings occur near Camden Avenue in block 113. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches are drawn in Camden Avenue and down Holly, Pine and Cedar Avenues, with fire hydrants at the corners. The ground east of Boulevard Avenue and below Maple Heights Avenue is open and marked as no exposure. Street widths of 45 feet are noted on most streets. The sheet adjoins sheet 14 across Camden Avenue, sheet 5 to the west and sheet 10 to the south.
notes: Camden Avenue is today East Main Street; Maple Heights Avenue is Maple Heights Road; Holly, Pine and Cedar Avenues are South Holly, South Pine and South Cedar Avenue.
The diagonal Boulevard Avenue at the lower right is today part of South Boulevard Avenue.
Drawn at 50 feet to an inch, unlike the 100 ft outlying sheets.
50 ft to an inch. East Main Street (old Camden Av) to Maple Heights Av and the diagonal Boulevard Av; Holly, Pine, Cedar, Boulevard Avs. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-7-1.description: The main part of sheet 7 shows the west side of Maple Shade from Broadway south to Gradwell Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Broadway and the parallel track of the C. & B.C. R.R. (P.R.R.) run along the top, with Front Avenue below them. North of Camden Avenue the cross streets are Seaside Avenue (marked not opened), Coles Avenue, Evergreen Avenue and Terrace Avenue, with Euclid Avenue running west from Coles Avenue; blocks 81, 83, 85 and 86 are thinly built with dwellings, coops and a woodworking and electric motor shop. Along Camden Avenue stand two gasoline stations, stores and a cinder block building. South of Camden Avenue a newer subdivision of long narrow lots lies between the diagonal Coles Avenue, Clinton Avenue, Terrace Avenue, Allen Avenue and Lippincott Avenue, crossed by Ethel, Nagel, Helen, Anna and Gradwell (Herbert) Avenues; several of these are marked not opened, and blocks 209 to 213 east of Terrace Avenue have few buildings. A small stream crosses Camden Avenue under a concrete bridge near Seaside Avenue and another runs south across the subdivision to Gradwell Avenue. Dwellings are frame with garages, with a few stores near the crossroads. The lower left corner of the sheet holds a separately framed inset (part 2) of the ground west of Seaside Avenue. Water pipes run in Camden Avenue, Coles, Clinton and Terrace Avenues, and Euclid Avenue.
notes: Camden Avenue is today West Main Street; Front Avenue is West Front Street; Broadway is West Broadway.
Evergreen Avenue (north of Camden Avenue) is today North Clinton Avenue; Ethel Avenue west of Clinton Avenue is today Anna Avenue.
The sheet's Helen Avenue (between Terrace and Lippincott Avenues) is today Nagle Avenue, and its Nagel Avenue is today Helen Avenue: the two names have been exchanged.
The West Main Street junctions at Seaside, Clinton and Lippincott Avenues lay 4.6 to 4.8 m from the fit and were excluded.
The railroad along Broadway is labelled C. & B.C. R.R. (P.R.R.).

100 ft to an inch. Two parts: 1 main map (Broadway to Gradwell Av, Seaside to Lippincott Av); 2 inset at lower left, the area west of Seaside Av to Pennsauken Creek (Front, Euclid, Camden Avs), same scale and orientation. Evergreen Av = North Clinton Avenue, Ethel Av = Anna Avenue; the sheet labels Helen Av and Nagel Av are today Nagle Avenue and Helen Avenue (swapped).

sheet-7-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 7 is a framed inset in the lower left corner, drawn at the same 100 feet to an inch and the same orientation as the main part. It shows the west end of the Front Avenue, Euclid Avenue and Camden Avenue blocks between Seaside Avenue and Pensauken Creek, the township line, continuing the main map westwards. Broadway and the C. & B.C. R.R. (P.R.R.) cross the top of the inset over a concrete bridge on the creek, Front Avenue lies below, and Camden Avenue crosses the creek on another concrete bridge at the bottom. Euclid Avenue is marked not opened west of Seaside Avenue, and Seaside Avenue itself is marked not opened. Blocks 81 and 82 are divided into lots but nearly empty: a few dwellings and garages stand on Camden Avenue and Front Avenue, and a sewage pumping station of concrete block stands in the open ground west of the lots. A large part of the inset is swamp land along the creek, crossed by a branch of Pensauken Creek; Chester Township lies on the east bank and Delaware Township on the west. The top of the inset is marked no exposure. The part was placed from two points carried from the main part (the Euclid Avenue and Camden Avenue junctions with Seaside Avenue), since the only modern junction it shows is Seaside Avenue at West Main Street.
notes: Camden Avenue is today West Main Street.
Placed from two points carried from sheet 7 part 1 (low confidence); the modern West Main Street junction at Seaside Avenue lies 4.6 m from part 1's fit.
Pensauken is spelled with one n on the sheet.

100 ft to an inch. Two parts: 1 main map (Broadway to Gradwell Av, Seaside to Lippincott Av); 2 inset at lower left, the area west of Seaside Av to Pennsauken Creek (Front, Euclid, Camden Avs), same scale and orientation. Evergreen Av = North Clinton Avenue, Ethel Av = Anna Avenue; the sheet labels Helen Av and Nagel Av are today Nagle Avenue and Helen Avenue (swapped).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the western and southern parts of Maple Shade south of Helen Avenue at 100 feet to an inch. At the left a regular grid between Lippincott Avenue and Fork Landing Road is divided by Helen Avenue, Anna Avenue, Gradwell Avenue and Thomas Avenue into blocks of single dwellings, outbuildings and coops, with lot numbers lettered along the street lines. Fork Landing Road runs north to south in the middle, then bends southwest toward Center Avenue, which crosses the lower part of the sheet from lower left to upper right and is the long southern boundary of the built area. East of Fork Landing Road a group of streets runs diagonally: East Avenue, Elm Avenue and Crawford Avenue (marked not open in part), Maple Avenue and Spruce Avenue, with dwellings, coops and large vacant lots. In the lower left Thomas Avenue (marked not open) and Frederick Avenue cut across blocks and several lots are shown as large unsubdivided parcels. West of Lippincott Avenue the sheet shows only the ends of streets drawn on Sheet 7 (Helen, Anna and Gradwell Avenues), and a blue stream appears at the left edge. Water pipes are marked in most streets. The compass rose and north arrow are at the right and the scale bar and Map Division stamp at the bottom.
notes: Scale bar reads 100 ft to one inch; fitted scale about 3.94 px/ft, rotation about 8 degrees.
Lippincott Avenue is now South Lippincott Avenue, Fork Landing Road is South Forklanding Road, East Avenue is East Gradwell Avenue and Center Avenue is East and West Center Avenue.

Anna Avenue / South Forklanding Road (4.5 m) and Gradwell Avenue / South Forklanding Road (3.2 m) were excluded as outliers; the modern Forklanding Road is a different alignment south of Center Avenue.
Margaret Street appears at the top of the sheet as a short street ending at Helen Avenue.
100 ft to an inch. West grid: Lippincott Av to Fork Landing Rd, Helen to Center Av (Thomas, Elm, Crawford, Frederick Avs); one part. Anna and Gradwell at South Forklanding left out.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the southern edge of the built-up area of Maple Shade at 100 feet to an inch, and is drawn turned about 50 degrees from north, with the streets running nearly vertically on the page. Center Avenue runs across the top, Mill Road crosses the middle and County Avenue forms the bottom edge. Fork Landing Road runs diagonally from the top centre down to the left, then vertically along the lower left; Sunset Avenue, Crawford Avenue, Elm Avenue and Maple Avenue run north and south across the sheet, with Buena Vista Avenue in the lower left. The blocks between Mill Road and County Avenue are mostly lots of dwellings with large coops and several greenhouses, including the Frank Matschke greenhouses at the lower right. North of Mill Road are large lots with scattered dwellings and the Joseph Schlitz, Inc., garage and bus repairing shop. Birch Avenue crosses a large irregular tract at the upper left, where the Chas. L. Pulk Sr. concrete block works stands among sheds. Street widths of 50 feet are marked on most streets and water pipes lettered along them. The compass rose and a long north arrow sit at the left; the scale bar and Map Division stamp are at the bottom.
notes: Scale bar reads 100 ft to one inch; fitted scale about 3.97 px/ft, rotation about 51 degrees (north arrow points up and right).
Center Avenue is East and West Center Avenue, Mill Road is East and West Mill Road, Fork Landing Road is South Forklanding Road, Maple Avenue is South Maple Avenue.
Modern Forklanding Road follows a different course south of Center Avenue; the drawn road runs southwest.
The node pair at Forklanding Road and West Mill Road is 14 m apart in OpenStreetMap; the western one was excluded as a duplicate.
100 ft to an inch, turned about 51 degrees. Mill Rd to County Av around Fork Landing Rd, Sunset, Buena Vista, Crawford, Elm Avs; one part.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the south-eastern part of Maple Shade, a built-up grid drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 52 degrees from north, so that the north arrow points to the upper right. The north-west block, between Center Avenue along the top edge and Mill Road, is laid out in long lots on Maple, Spruce and Poplar Avenues, with scattered frame dwellings and coops. South of Mill Road a large tract (159) with a large brick dwelling and a cinder-block outbuilding lies between Maple and Harned Avenues, and a regular row of dwellings fronts Harned Avenue. Fellowship Road runs diagonally down the middle of the sheet, 45 to 50 feet wide, with an American Legion club on its east side. East of Fellowship Road the blocks (144 to 151) are bounded by Boulevard Avenue, Center Avenue, Barlow, Bailey and Salmon Avenues and Foster Avenue, mostly with dwellings and some streets marked as not opened. A small diagonal subdivision of Holly Avenue and Pine Avenue (blocks 140 to 142) lies in the angle north of Boulevard Avenue. Irving Avenue closes the sheet at the bottom, with blocks 220 to 226 below it. Six-inch and four-inch water pipes are marked in most streets. The upper right is blank apart from the compass rose and title cartouche; adjoining sheets are numbered 4, 5, 6 and 9.
notes: Maple Av is South Maple Avenue today; Harned Av (south of Mill Road) is the line of Spruce Avenue.
Boulevard Av east of Fellowship Road and Mill Rd are both East Mill Road today; Barlow Av is South Pine Avenue; the sheet's east-west Center Av south of Mill Road is Salmon Avenue.
Irving Av is County Avenue in the modern data, but County Avenue is displaced from the drawn line at three junctions (5 to 9 m) and was left out of the fit.
Read at moderate confidence: Walnut Avenue and Cedar Avenue (small diagonal streets) and the absence of a printed prefix on Holly and Pine Avenue.

100 ft to an inch, turned about 53 degrees. Maple, Spruce (Harned), Poplar, Fellowship, Pine (Barlow), Bailey, Salmon Avs around Mill Rd and Center Av; one part. County Avenue (sheet Irving Av) left out, 5-9 m off.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows a thinly built part of western Maple Shade at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that the north arrow points to the upper right. Center Avenue runs along the bottom edge, with Martin, Alexander, Buttonwood, Cutler and Frederick Avenues meeting it from the north; the neighbouring sheet 12 lies below, 13 to the left, 7 to the upper right and 8 to the right. Most of the sheet is open land divided into large numbered tracts (84, 117, 118, 119, 213, 214, 217, 218) and long narrow lots, with dwellings scattered mainly along the edges. Coles Avenue crosses the upper left and Clinton (Vorhees) Avenue the centre, both running south-west to north-east; Frederick Avenue runs diagonally from the lower right up to Clinton Avenue, and Thomas Avenue and Lippincott Avenue serve a denser group of frame dwellings in block 118 at the right. Stinson Avenue and several streets marked not opened cross the open tracts. Along the upper right Gradwell (Herbert) Avenue and Allen Avenue meet a small stream, a branch of the creek system shown on sheet 7. Six-inch water pipes run in Coles, Clinton, Thomas and Frederick Avenues and in Center Avenue. Rows of narrow building lots are laid out along Center Avenue and between Martin and Buttonwood Avenues but only partly built on.
notes: Coles Av, Clinton Av and Lippincott Av are South Coles Avenue, South Clinton Avenue and South Lippincott Avenue today; Center Av is West Center Avenue; Gradwell (Herbert) Av is Gradwell Avenue.
Allen Avenue and Stinson Avenue are not in the modern street data; Buttonwood Avenue jogs about 115 feet across Center Avenue on the sheet and its junction was left out of the fit.
The fit places all junctions at 1.4 to 2.9 m; the sheet is probably drawn with some distortion.
100 ft to an inch, turned about 54 degrees. Subdivision between Coles, Clinton (Vorhees), Thomas, Frederick, Alexander, Stinson Avs and Center Av; one part.

sheet-12-1.description: The main part of sheet 12 covers the thinly built southwest of Maple Shade from Center Avenue south past Mill Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 52 degrees, so that north points to the upper right. Center Avenue runs along the top, with Buttonwood Avenue and Frederick Avenue named in the margin beyond it. Martin Avenue runs down the left side and bends diagonally to meet Alexander Avenue and Mill Road at a five-way junction; Alexander Avenue continues south to the bottom of the sheet, and Buttonwood Avenue and Cutler Avenue run from Center Avenue to Mill Road. Birch Avenue is named at the right edge. The blocks, numbered 126 to 131 and 162 and 163, are large and mostly empty, with scattered frame dwellings, garages and many chicken coops. Below Mill Road the South Branch of Pensauken Creek winds across the lower left, with Chester Township on the near side and Delaware Township beyond it. A dash-dot match line A to B near the bottom marks where the lower right inset (part 2) continues Alexander and Buttonwood Avenues. Water pipes are drawn in Center Avenue, Martin Avenue, Alexander Avenue, Cutler Avenue and Mill Road, and part of Martin Avenue is marked not opened.
notes: Center Avenue is today West Center Avenue; Mill Road is West Mill Road.
Sheet turned about 52 degrees; the north arrow points to the upper right.

100 ft to an inch, turned about 52 degrees. Two parts: 1 main map (Center Av to below Mill Rd, Martin to Cutler Av); 2 inset at lower right continuing Alexander and Buttonwood Avs south of match line A-B to Rudderow Av, Pennsauken Creek South Branch.

sheet-12-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 12 is a framed inset in the lower right quarter of the sheet that continues the main map beyond the match line A to B. It shows Alexander Avenue and Buttonwood Avenue running south from that line to Rudderow Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and at the same turned orientation as the main part, with its own north arrow pointing to the upper right. Alexander Avenue bends where it leaves the frame lines and meets Rudderow Avenue, which runs east from it near the bottom. Block 162 between the two avenues is divided into long lots with only a few dwellings, garages and coops; block 163, west of Alexander Avenue, is open ground along the South Branch of Pensauken Creek, which winds down the left side of the inset between Chester Township and Delaware Township. A few dwellings stand south of Rudderow Avenue in block 165. Water pipes are drawn in Alexander Avenue and Buttonwood Avenue. The inset was placed from two points carried across the match line from the main part, one junction found by the detector (Buttonwood Avenue West at West Rudderow Avenue) and one hand-picked junction (Alexander Avenue at West Rudderow Avenue).
notes: Buttonwood Avenue south of Mill Road is today Buttonwood Avenue West; Rudderow Avenue is West Rudderow Avenue.
Fitted scale 4 percent larger than the main part; four control points, two of them carried.

100 ft to an inch, turned about 52 degrees. Two parts: 1 main map (Center Av to below Mill Rd, Martin to Cutler Av); 2 inset at lower right continuing Alexander and Buttonwood Avs south of match line A-B to Rudderow Av, Pennsauken Creek South Branch.

sheet-13-1.description: The main part of sheet 13 covers the south of Maple Shade between Mill Road and Rudderow Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 52 degrees. Buttonwood Avenue runs down the left side, Cutler Avenue through the middle and Fork Landing Road down the right of the main blocks, with County Avenue and Sunset Avenue in the lower right; Rudderow Avenue crosses the bottom. The largest building is Maple Shade Public School No. 3 on Mill Road between Cutler Avenue and Fork Landing Road, of fireproof construction, built 1925, with steam heat and electric lights. Otherwise the blocks, numbered 158 to 161 and 164, are large and thinly built: frame dwellings and garages, many chicken coops, and open lots, with a row of small houses on Sunset Avenue in block 159. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in Mill Road, Buttonwood Avenue, Cutler Avenue, Fork Landing Road and County Avenue, with hydrants at the corners. The ground beyond Sunset Avenue at the right edge is marked no exposure. The upper right quarter of the sheet is a separately framed inset (part 2) showing Florence and Rynning Avenues near Coles Avenue, a different place.
notes: Mill Road is today West and East Mill Road; Fork Landing Road is South Forklanding Road; Rudderow Avenue is West and East Rudderow Avenue.
Maple Shade Public School No. 3, built 1925.
Fork Landing Road junctions carry 2.6 to 3.3 m residuals; the modern road may not follow the old line exactly.

100 ft to an inch. Two parts: 1 main map (Mill Rd to Rudderow Av, Buttonwood Av to Sunset Av, Maple Shade Public School No. 3); 2 inset at upper right, Florence and Rynning Avs west of Coles Av down to Pennsauken Creek South Branch (Delaware Township).

sheet-13-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 13 is a framed inset in the upper right of the sheet, with its own north arrow pointing nearly straight up; it shows a place on the west side of town, not the ground next to the main part. Florence Avenue runs across its top and Rynning Avenue across its middle, both ending at Coles Avenue on the right; Clinton Avenue and Alexander Avenue are named in the margin beyond Coles Avenue. Block 215 between the two avenues is laid out in lots with frame dwellings, garages and coops, a few of them brick or concrete. South of Rynning Avenue block 216 runs down to the creek: its upper lots hold a few dwellings, and the lower ground is swamp land along the South Branch of Pensauken Creek, which crosses the inset and passes under Coles Avenue at a concrete bridge. The township line follows the creek, with Chester Township on the north side and Delaware Township to the south. Water pipes are drawn in Florence Avenue, Rynning Avenue and Coles Avenue. The part was placed from two junctions on Coles Avenue only, Florence Avenue (detected) and Rynning Avenue (hand-picked), so its rotation rests on the line of Coles Avenue.
notes: Coles Avenue is today South Coles Avenue.
Two-point helmert placement on Coles Avenue (low confidence).

100 ft to an inch. Two parts: 1 main map (Mill Rd to Rudderow Av, Buttonwood Av to Sunset Av, Maple Shade Public School No. 3); 2 inset at upper right, Florence and Rynning Avs west of Coles Av down to Pennsauken Creek South Branch (Delaware Township).

sheet-14-1.description: The lower part of Sheet 14 is the south half of a two-strip sheet drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It lies below the heavy railroad line that crosses the sheet, between the not-opened Broadway and Front Avenue at the top and Camden Avenue at the bottom, and runs east from Holly Avenue to the Pensauken Creek branch and the Moorestown Township line. Holly, Pine, Cedar and Boulevard Avenues run down to Camden Avenue, with numbered blocks 95, 96, 206, 207 and 208 between them. The Maple Shade Brick Co. Inc. plant (kilns, a dryer, brick moulding shed, clay pile and brick piles) stands in the centre. Cedar Avenue carries a row of cinder-block dwellings and a stand pipe stands to its west. Palmyra and Berlin Road (S-41) crosses diagonally at the right, and beyond it lie the Chester Township Municipal Water Works with a pumping station, filter house and settling basin. A dashed railroad branch runs parallel to the heavy line along the top. Below Camden Avenue the streets continue as Pine, Cedar and Boulevard Avenues towards sheet 6, with a Public Service sub-station at lower right. The scale bar and a Map Division stamp occupy the lower margin. The upper strip of the sheet, west of Holly Avenue and north of Camden Avenue, is described as part 2.
notes: The lower strip repeats the Holly Avenue to Front Avenue to Camden Avenue band east of the upper strip; Camden Avenue is East Main Street today and the streets north of it are North Holly, North Pine, North Cedar and North Boulevard Avenue.
Control is from Camden Avenue (East Main Street) junctions only, so rotation rests on one line; Front Avenue and Broadway are not opened here and gave junctions 4 m off.
Palmyra & Berlin Road is NJ 73 today, a rebuilt highway not used for control.

100 ft to an inch. Two parts divided by the heavy line along the railroad: 1 lower strip (Holly Av to Pensauken Creek, Broadway to Camden Av; Maple Shade Brick Co., Chester Township Municipal Water Works), placed by a helmert on East Main Street only (low confidence); 2 upper strip (Poplar to Holly Av, Broadway to Camden Av; Maple Shade Public School No. 2).

sheet-14-2.description: The upper part of Sheet 14 shows the north side of Maple Shade between Poplar Avenue on the west and Holly Avenue on the east, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned slightly from north. Camden Avenue forms the lower edge, just above the heavy railroad line, with Front Avenue and Broadway and the tracks of the C. and B. C. R.R. and P. R. R. along the top. Poplar Avenue, Fellowship Road (drawn on a slant), Chestnut Avenue, Stiles Avenue and Holly Avenue run north to south between them, enclosing blocks 91 to 94. Houses are mostly frame dwellings on narrow lots along Poplar, Stiles and Holly Avenues, with Maple Shade Public School No. 2 (a brick building) between Fellowship Road and Chestnut Avenue and a garage and repair shop at Poplar Avenue and Camden Avenue. Large areas between Front Avenue and the rear of the lots are open. Below Camden Avenue, along the railroad, the sheet letters Spruce Avenue, Poplar Avenue, Cherry Avenue and Walnut Avenue where they meet the line. Virginia Avenue appears at the top, and neighbouring sheets are numbered 3, 4, 5, 14, 15, 16 and 17. The lower strip east of Holly Avenue is described as part 1.
notes: Camden Avenue is East Main Street today; Poplar, Fellowship, Chestnut, Stiles and Holly Avenues are the North-prefixed streets of those names; Front Avenue and Broadway are East Front Street and East Broadway.
The railroad crossing at Stiles Avenue was not used for control because track layouts have changed.

100 ft to an inch. Two parts divided by the heavy line along the railroad: 1 lower strip (Holly Av to Pensauken Creek, Broadway to Camden Av; Maple Shade Brick Co., Chester Township Municipal Water Works), placed by a helmert on East Main Street only (low confidence); 2 upper strip (Poplar to Holly Av, Broadway to Camden Av; Maple Shade Public School No. 2).

sheet-15-1.description: The main part of sheet 15 covers the north side of Maple Shade between Woodlawn Avenue and the railroad, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 30 degrees. Broadway, the C. & B.C. R.R. and Front Avenue run diagonally across the lower part, with Linwood Avenue and Park Avenue parallel to them further north and Woodlawn Avenue at the top right. The cross streets are Coles Avenue on the left, Elmwood Avenue, Melrose Avenue and Oakland Avenue in the middle, and Fork Landing Road on the right edge, where Beechwood Avenue and Mecray Lane are named. Evergreen Avenue and Terrace Avenue are named at the bottom where they reach Front Avenue. The blocks, numbered 27 to 30, 42 to 45 and 65 to 75, are filled with frame dwellings and garages, closer together towards Broadway, with a few stores near Fork Landing Road. Industry is represented by the M.S.W. Products Co. cinder block manufactory with its drying and mold yard at the west end of Park Avenue, and the large greenhouses of C. F. Graythorn on Elmwood Avenue. The top of the sheet holds a framed inset (part 2) of the Wm. Graham Brick Company, and the lower left corner a small framed inset of the west end of Linwood Avenue (part 3, not placed).
notes: Fork Landing Road is today North Forklanding Road; Park and Woodlawn Avenues are West Park and West Woodlawn Avenue; Coles Avenue is North Coles Avenue.
Broadway, Linwood Avenue and Front Avenue junctions lay 5 to 15 m from the fit and were left out (RMSE 2.6 to 0.8 m without them).
C. F. Graythorn greenhouses; M.S.W. Products Co. cinder block manufactory.

100 ft to an inch. Three parts: 1 main map (Woodlawn Av to Broadway and Front Av, Coles Av to Fork Landing Rd); 2 inset at top, Wm. Graham Brick Company between Pine Av and Palmyra & Berlin Rd (S-41) on the C. & B.C. R.R.; 3 small inset at lower left, the west end of Linwood Av (not placed).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: west end of Linwood Avenue (blocks 65 and 73) (no street junction; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-15-1 or sheet-16).

sheet-15-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 15 is a framed inset across the top of the sheet showing the works of the Wm. Graham Brick Company on the north side of the railroad east of Maple Shade, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow. Pine Avenue runs down the left side across Broadway and Front Avenue, and Palmyra & Berlin Road (S-41) crosses the right side diagonally; between them the C. & B.C. R.R. (P.R.R.) runs straight across the inset with a railroad siding branching off near the road. The brick works, in block 205, consist of kilns, two dryers and a clay moulding building with an engine room, with brick piles beside them and a large clay quarry to the east; the notes say it has no watchman, steam power, no light and no heat. A dwelling and a shed stand on Pine Avenue at the top left, and the ground east of Palmyra & Berlin Road is block 233. Road widths of 46 and 80 feet are noted. The inset was placed from the junction of Broadway and Pine Avenue alone, at the atlas scale, with its rotation taken from the drawn lines there; the road and the railroad agree with that rotation, while the modern NJ 73 crossing would have stretched the part by about 5 percent.
notes: Pine Avenue north of Front Avenue is today Pine Road; Palmyra & Berlin Road (S-41) is today NJ 73, rebuilt as a divided highway.
The railroad is labelled C. & B.C. R.R. (P.R.R.); it is today the Pemberton Industrial Track.
Anchored on one junction with the atlas scale (low confidence).

100 ft to an inch. Three parts: 1 main map (Woodlawn Av to Broadway and Front Av, Coles Av to Fork Landing Rd); 2 inset at top, Wm. Graham Brick Company between Pine Av and Palmyra & Berlin Rd (S-41) on the C. & B.C. R.R.; 3 small inset at lower left, the west end of Linwood Av (not placed).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: west end of Linwood Avenue (blocks 65 and 73) (no street junction; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-15-1 or sheet-16).

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers the north-western part of Maple Shade on the line of Fork Landing Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 8 degrees from the sheet edges (the printed compass rose at upper left points straight up). Broadway, with the tracks of the C. & B. C. R.R. and P. R. R. and Maple Shade Station beneath it, closes the bottom of the main map; Station Avenue and Front Avenue run below it and are drawn on the neighbouring sheet 3. The densest development is the lower block between Park Avenue and Broadway, where Linwood Avenue crosses Maple Avenue and Fellowship Road; blocks 68, 69, 76 and 77 hold frame dwellings in rows, St. John's P. E. Church stands in block 68 and a small cluster of industrial or storage buildings with blue (non-combustible) roofs lies beside Fork Landing Road. North of Mecray Lane the grid turns to run north-west, and large blocks 46 to 51 and 56 to 58 along Walnut, Fernwood, Maple, Greenwood, Glendale and Laurelton Avenues carry only scattered dwellings and a woodworking shop (A. Levin) at the upper right. Several streets are marked not open. Water pipes run in most streets. Neighbouring sheets are 3, 14, 15, 17 and 18.
notes: Walnut Av is Lincoln Avenue today; Maple Av is North Maple Avenue, Linwood Av is East Linwood Avenue, Park Av is East Park Avenue, Woodlawn Av is East Woodlawn Avenue, Laurelton Av is East Laurelton Avenue and Fork Landing Rd is North Forklanding Road.
Front Avenue, Station Avenue and the bottom edge below Broadway belong to sheet 3 and were not used for control; East Front Street junctions were rejected at 7.5 m.
Poplar Avenue is read from a small label at the bottom edge; medium confidence.
100 ft to an inch. Fork Landing Rd to Fellowship Rd, Woodlawn Av to Broadway; one part. Walnut Av = Lincoln Avenue.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 shows the north-eastern part of Maple Shade at 100 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned about 9 degrees from the sheet edges and the compass rose at left. Broadway and the C. & B. C. R.R. and P. R. R. tracks run along the bottom, and the sheet extends north through Park Avenue, Yale Avenue and Harvard Avenue to Swarthmore Avenue at the top, where it meets sheet 19 (Cinnaminson Township). Stiles Avenue is the main north-south street, with Virginia Avenue, Fellowship Road, Laurelton Avenue and Glendale Avenue to its west and Pine Avenue (Sauselein) on the east. The most built-up area is the lower strip between Park Avenue and Broadway, where blocks 62, 63, 70, 71, 72, 78, 79 and 80 hold rows of frame dwellings; the Pen-i-Sauken Silk Mill (warping, winding and weaving rooms, night watchman and steam, electric light) stands in block 71 beside Virginia Avenue, and a long U-shaped group of coops occupies block 72. The Palmyra & Berlin Road (S-41) crosses the upper right diagonally. A branch of Pensauken Creek runs down the right edge to a pond-like widening. The remaining blocks (52 to 55, 59, 60, 64, 232, 233) are largely open with scattered dwellings, and several streets are marked not open. A scale bar and the Map Division stamp sit at the lower right.
notes: Swarthmore Av is East Woodlawn Avenue today, Yale Av continues Mecray Lane, Pine (Sauselein) Av is Pine Road, and Palmyra & Berlin Road is NJ 73; the others are North Stiles Avenue, East Linwood Avenue and East Park Avenue.
NJ 73 was not used for control; the Fellowship Road and Mecray Lane junction (3.9 m) and Laurelton and Mecray Lane (6.8 m) were left out.
Stream name read as North Branch, Pensauken Creek, from small lettering along the creek; medium confidence. The suffix of Pine (Sauselein) is read from the overview; medium confidence.
100 ft to an inch. Laurelton and Stiles Avs to the North Branch of Pensauken Creek, Swarthmore Av to Broadway, Pen-I-Sauken Silk Mill; one part. Swarthmore Av = East Woodlawn Avenue.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the northern edge of the built-up part of Maple Shade, where the town meets Cinnaminson Township (sheet 19 lies above and to the right). It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 30 degrees from north. Fork Landing Road runs down the left edge and Palmyra & Berlin Road (S-41) down the right edge. Orchard Avenue, 5th Avenue, Germantown Avenue and Woodlawn Avenue cross the sheet from side to side and enclose large numbered blocks (23 to 26, 31 to 37) that are mostly open land with scattered frame dwellings and coops; several lots in block 23 have blue-roofed non-combustible dwellings beside Fork Landing Road. Only the lower strip between Germantown Avenue and Woodlawn Avenue is laid out in narrow lots, along Walnut, Fernwood, Maple and Greenwood Avenues, with a diagonal property line cutting across the lower left. At lower right a large tract is marked Picnic Grounds, Herman Dunsky, with a store and dwelling, bounded by Glendale Avenue, Cedar Lane (not open) and Laurelton Avenue. Linden Avenue continues Greenwood Avenue north of Germantown Avenue. Peach Avenue and Fernwood Avenue appear at the top, with Haverford Avenue and Swarthmore Avenue at the right edge. The compass rose and scale bar lie in the lower middle; sheet 16 is below.
notes: Woodlawn Av is East Woodlawn Avenue today, Walnut Av is Lincoln Avenue, Linden Av is the line of Greenwood Avenue, Fork Landing Rd is North Forklanding Road, Germantown Av is East Germantown Avenue, and Palmyra & Berlin Road is NJ 73.
NJ 73 was not used for control.
Peach Avenue is partly cut off at the top edge and read from the overview; medium confidence. Picnic Grounds is listed as a place name though it is a private tract (Herman Dunsky).

100 ft to an inch, turned about 31 degrees. Orchard Av to Woodlawn Av, Fork Landing Rd to Laurelton Av and Palmyra & Berlin Rd, picnic grounds; one part. Linden Av = Greenwood Avenue north of Germantown Av.

sheet-19-1.description: The main part of sheet 19 covers the north end of Maple Shade and the adjoining part of Cinnaminson Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 29 degrees. Fork Landing Road runs up the left side, with Jordantown Road branching off at the upper left; Palmyra & Berlin Road (S-41) runs diagonally down the right side. Between them High and Orchard Avenue cross the sheet, and Fernwood (Apple) Avenue, Peach Avenue and Cherry Avenue run north to south; Cherry Avenue is marked not opened, and Linden Avenue is named below Orchard Avenue at the bottom. The dash-dot boundary between Cinnaminson Township and Chester Township crosses the upper half of the sheet. The blocks, numbered 17 to 22, are large and thinly built with frame dwellings, garages, greenhouses and many chicken coops, and a button manufactory stands on Fork Landing Road in block 20. The ground beyond Fork Landing Road and beyond Palmyra & Berlin Road is marked no exposure. The top of the sheet, set off by a heavy line, is a separately drawn part (part 2) of the streets around Haverford and Swarthmore Avenues. The upper half of this part has no control point, so its placement there is extrapolated from junctions on High and Orchard Avenue.
notes: Peach Avenue is today North Maple Avenue; High is High Street; Fork Landing Road is North Forklanding Road; Palmyra & Berlin Road (S-41) is NJ 73.
High Street / North Maple Avenue was hand-picked from the block corners; the detector had taken Peach Avenue's west edge, 40 ft off.
No control in the upper half of the part.

100 ft to an inch. Two parts divided by a heavy line: 1 main map (Fork Landing Rd to Palmyra & Berlin Rd, Cinnaminson/Chester Township line, High St, Orchard Av; Peach Av = North Maple Avenue); 2 upper part (Haverford and Swarthmore Avs, Laurelton and Stiles Avs, Cinnaminson Township).

sheet-19-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 19 is the top strip of the sheet, set off from the main part by a heavy line and drawn with its own north arrow pointing straight up. It shows a grid in Cinnaminson Township north of the township line: Haverford Avenue and Swarthmore Avenue run across it, Laurelton Avenue and Stiles Avenue run north to south, and Palmyra & Berlin Road (S-41) cuts diagonally across the left half; Cornell Avenue is named at the top, Cedar Lane beside the heavy line and Woodlawn Avenue at the lower left. The blocks, numbered 38 to 41 and 230 and 231, are laid out in narrow lots with a scattering of frame dwellings, garages and coops; much of the ground is still empty. Water pipes are drawn in Haverford Avenue and Stiles Avenue. A small stretch of a creek appears at the top right corner. The part was placed from four junctions of Haverford and Swarthmore Avenues with Laurelton and Stiles Avenues.
notes: Swarthmore Avenue is today East Woodlawn Avenue; Laurelton Avenue is East Laurelton Avenue; Stiles Avenue is North Stiles Avenue; Palmyra & Berlin Road (S-41) is NJ 73.
Four control points; NJ 73 junctions not detected.

100 ft to an inch. Two parts divided by a heavy line: 1 main map (Fork Landing Rd to Palmyra & Berlin Rd, Cinnaminson/Chester Township line, High St, Orchard Av; Peach Av = North Maple Avenue); 2 upper part (Haverford and Swarthmore Avs, Laurelton and Stiles Avs, Cinnaminson Township).
